sections.heading: 1. Key Expressions & Sentences Reviewed (Lessons 15–21)
points: Lesson 15: "Ndikumbirewo kuti uvhura hwindo mhepo imbopinda mumba muno." — May I please ask you to open the window so some fresh air can come into the room.
Lesson 16: "Ndapota huyai muchinyararire nokuti murwere achangobatwa nehope." — Please come in quietly because the patient has just fallen asleep.
Lesson 17: "Manheru amai. nhasi ndakaneta asi zvinhu zvafamba zvakanaka hazvo." — Good evening, Mother. Today I am tired, but things went well nonetheless.
Lesson 18: "Mhoro shamwari yangu. wakafamba sei nezuro; wakasvika zvakanaka here?" — Hello my friend. How was your trip yesterday; did you arrive safely?
Lesson 19: "Ndapota tumira mashoko acho zvakare nokuti handina kuaverenga zvakanaka." — Please send the message again because I did not read it properly.
Lesson 20: "Mangwanani. Ndamuka zvakanaka nhasi; ndirikugadzirira kuenda kusvondo." — Good morning. I woke up well today; I am getting ready to go to church.
Lesson 21: "Takatenga hupfu, shuga, mafuta, nemuriwo." — We bought maize meal, sugar, cooking oil, and vegetables.

sections.heading: 2. Core Shona Grammar Rules Consolidated
points: Talking About Location: 'pa-', 'ku-', and 'mu-' ('mumba'): pa- = on / at a point (patafura) | ku- = to / at a place (kuchikoro) | mu- = inside (mumba)
Giving Commands & Polite Requests ('huyai'): Singular Command: Verb stem (-a) [Huya! / Tora!] | Polite or Plural Command: Verb stem + -i (-ai) [Huyai! / Torai!]
Shona Greetings & Time of Day ('Manheru'): Morning: Mangwanani | Afternoon: Masikati | Evening: Manheru | How are you?: Makadini? / Wakadii?
Shona Greetings & Time of Day ('Mhoro'): Morning: Mangwanani | Afternoon: Masikati | Evening: Manheru | How are you?: Makadini? / Wakadii?
Talking About the Past ('zvakare'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Shona Greetings & Time of Day ('Mangwanani'): Morning: Mangwanani | Afternoon: Masikati | Evening: Manheru | How are you?: Makadini? / Wakadii?

sections.heading: 3. Cultural Context & Practical Usage
points: Fresh Highveld Breeze ('Mhepo') & Home Ventilation: Because most of Zimbabwe sits on a sunny subtropical plateau between 1,200 and 1,600 metres above sea level, homes are designed with wide windows ('mahwindo') that are opened during the day to let in cool, refreshing breezes ('mhepo')..

Visiting the Sick ('ushanya Murwere') & Quiet Consideration: Visiting an ill relative or neighbour ('murwere') to offer comfort is a core duty in Shona culture ('kubata maoko' / 'kutarisa murwere'), and visitors enter quietly ('muchinyararire') whenever the patient has just fallen asleep ('achangobatwa nehope')..

Evening Check-Ins with Mother ('Manheru Amai') After Work: Returning home in the evening begins with a respectful greeting to one's parents ('Manheru amai') and a reassuring report on the day's work: even when tired ('ndakaneta'), adding 'zvinhu zvafamba zvakanaka hazvo' ('things went well nonetheless') expresses gratitude and resilience..

Following Up on a Friend's Journey ('Wakafamba Sei?'): Among friends ('shamwari'), asking 'Wakafamba sei nezuro; wakasvika zvakanaka here?' ('How did you travel yesterday; did you arrive safely?') is the standard warm follow-up the day after someone has taken an intercity bus or road trip..

review_exercises.prompt: Review 3 — Family & Present Progressive: How do you say 'My friends are studying in the house'?
review_exercises.explanation: Plural 'shamwari dzangu' ('my friends') takes 'dziri ku-' + '-dzidza' ('are studying') + 'mumba' ('in the house').

review_exercises.prompt: Review 3 — 'Before' Clauses ('-sati'): How do you say 'Let me rest a little before I cook'?
review_exercises.explanation: 'Ndisati ndabika' literally means 'before I have cooked'.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 3 — School & Exams: What does 'kupasa bvunzo dzekupedzisira' mean?
options: to read a short story in class
to bring our books to school tomorrow
to ask the teacher a question

review_exercises.prompt: Review 3 — Giving Reasons ('nokuti'): Complete the sentence: 'Tiri kutaura tichizevezera ______ mwana akarara.' (We are speaking in whispers because the baby is asleep.)
Review 3 — Laundry & Household Chores: If you say 'Mbatya dzangu dzaoma panze', what happened to your clothes?
options: My clothes are still wet in the house
I will wash my clothes tomorrow morning
I bought new clothes at the market

review_exercises.prompt: Review 3 — Translate this new review sentence: 'Tichasangana naBaba kumusha svondo rinouya.'
options: We visited Grandmother at the clinic yesterday.
Mother is buying vegetables at the market today.
We will meet Father at the rural home next week.
My sibling is writing an essay at school.
review_exercises.correct_answer: We will meet Father at the rural home next week.
review_exercises.explanation: 'Tichasangana naBaba' = 'We will meet Father', 'kumusha' = 'at the rural home', 'svondo rinouya' = 'next week'.
